films.title: American Psycho
films.basedOn: American Psycho (1991 novel) by Bret Easton Ellis
films.villain: Patrick Bateman, a wealthy investment banker who leads a double life as a serial killer
notes: Premiered at Sundance on January 21, 2000; U.S./Canada release April 14, 2000
Satirizes 1980s yuppie culture and consumerism
Director Mary Harron was fired when Lions Gate wanted Leonardo DiCaprio instead of Christian Bale, and was replaced by Oliver Stone
Principal photography began February 1999 in Toronto and New York City
Followed by a direct-to-video sequel, American Psycho 2

films.title: Final Destination
films.writers: Glen Morgan, James Wong and Jeffrey Reddick
films.villain: Death itself, which kills those who escaped a plane explosion in the order they were meant to die
notes: James Wong's directorial debut
Story by Jeffrey Reddick
Principal photography in New York City and Vancouver, with additional scenes in Toronto and San Francisco
Characters are named after horror figures: Billy Hitchcock, Tod Waggner, Larry Murnau, Valerie Lewton, Agent Schreck
First sequel, Final Destination 2, released January 31, 2003

films.title: Scary Movie
films.writers: Shawn and Marlon Wayans and 4 others
films.villain: The Killer, a Ghostface-style slasher (Dave Sheridan plays Doofy Gilmore / The Killer)
notes: Parody of the slasher genre, mainly Scream and I Know What You Did Last Summer
Co-written by Jason Friedberg and Aaron Seltzer, plus Buddy Johnson and Phil Beauman
Released July 7, 2000 in the U.S.
Spawned five sequels starting with Scary Movie 2 (2001)

films.title: Ginger Snaps
films.yearNote: Premiered at Munich Fantasy Filmfest on August 1, 2000; wider release May 11, 2001
films.villain: A werewolf (the 'Beast of Bailey Downs') whose bite turns Ginger into the 'Gingerwolf'
notes: Canadian film; story developed jointly by John Fawcett and Karen Walton
Principal photography October 25 to December 6, 1999
Lucy Lawless has an uncredited cameo as a school announcer
Followed by Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed and prequel Ginger Snaps Back: The Beginning, both 2004

films.title: Battle Royale
films.basedOn: Battle Royale (1999 novel) by Koushun Takami
films.villain: An authoritarian government that forces a junior high class to fight to the death
notes: Released December 16, 2000 in Japan
Kinji Fukasaku died January 12, 2003 after shooting one scene of the sequel Battle Royale II: Requiem
Extended non-theatrical version adds an epilogue
Arrow Video issued a 4K restoration in April 2021

films.title: Pulse
films.villain: Ghosts invading the real world through the Internet, causing mass disappearances
notes: Released February 3, 2001 in Japan
Screened in Un Certain Regard at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival
Dimension Films acquired remake rights after Cannes; English remake Pulse released 2006 and produced two sequels

films.title: The Others
films.villain: Unseen presences in the house, which Grace believes are intruders haunting her family
notes: Written, directed and scored by Alejandro Amenábar
Children Anne and Nicholas are photosensitive, so the house is kept dark
Won three Saturn Awards at the 28th ceremony: Best Horror Film, Best Actress (Kidman), Best Supporting Actress (Flanagan)
Kidman was nominated for a Golden Globe for Best Actress – Drama
Released in the U.S. August 10, 2001 and in Spain September 7, 2001

films.title: Jeepers Creepers
films.villain: The Creeper, a monstrous winged creature who drives a truck and hunts siblings returning home
notes: Title comes from the 1938 song, heard in a Paul Whiteman version
Victor Salva was inspired to make a monster movie by Creature from the Black Lagoon (1954)
Salva makes a cameo appearance
Premiered at Fantasia July 28, 2001; U.S. release August 31, 2001
Spawned two sequels and a reboot

films.title: Thir13en Ghosts
films.writers: Neal Marshall Stevens and Richard D'Ovidio
films.basedOn: 13 Ghosts (1960 film) by Robb White
films.villain: Twelve captive ghosts (the Dark Zodiac) bound inside a house, used to power a machine
notes: Steve Beck's directorial debut
Remake of William Castle's 1960 film 13 Ghosts
Released October 26, 2001

films.title: From Hell
films.genreNote: historical slasher / Jack the Ripper thriller
films.director: The Hughes Brothers (Albert and Allen Hughes)
films.basedOn: From Hell (graphic novel) by Alan Moore and Eddie Campbell
films.villain: Jack the Ripper, revealed as Sir William Gull, a royal physician
notes: Loosely based on the Alan Moore and Eddie Campbell graphic novel
US/UK/Czech Republic co-production
Released October 19, 2001

films.title: Session 9
films.villain: Unknown force tied to the abandoned asylum and patient Mary Hobbes's recorded therapy sessions
notes: Follows an asbestos abatement crew working in abandoned Danvers State Psychiatric Hospital
Premiered at Fantasia Festival July 31, 2001; U.S. release August 10, 2001
Co-writer Stephen Gevedon also stars as Mike

films.title: Joy Ride
films.yearNote: Released as Road Kill in the UK and Roadkill in Australia
films.writers: Clay Tarver and J. J. Abrams
films.setting: Salt Lake City to Colorado highways
cast: Rusty Nail (physical; voiced by Ted Levine, uncredited)
films.villain: Rusty Nail, a psychopathic trucker they prank on their CB radio (voiced by Ted Levine)
notes: Screenplay co-written by J. J. Abrams
Principal photography in Nevada, California and Utah
Spawned direct-to-video sequels Joy Ride 2: Dead Ahead (2008) and Joy Ride 3: Roadkill (2014)

films.title: The Mothman Prophecies
films.basedOn: The Mothman Prophecies (1975 book) by John Keel
films.villain: The Mothman, a winged creature said to presage disasters
notes: Based on events between November 1966 and December 1967 in Point Pleasant, as described by John Keel
Shot in Pittsburgh and Kittanning, Pennsylvania
Released January 25, 2002; mixed reviews but has since gained a cult following

films.title: 28 Days Later
films.villain: The 'Rage' virus infected, plus Major West's soldiers
notes: Released in the UK on November 1, 2002
Most of the film was shot on Canon XL1 digital video cameras
Cillian Murphy plays a bicycle courier who wakes from a coma
Sequel 28 Weeks Later released May 11, 2007
Won a Saturn Award and an Empire Award for Best British Film

films.title: The Ring
films.basedOn: Ring (1998 film) / Ring (novel) by Koji Suzuki
films.villain: Samara Morgan, whose cursed videotape kills viewers seven days later
notes: Won Best Horror Film and Best Actress (Naomi Watts) at the 29th Saturn Awards
Its success inspired American remakes of Asian horror, including The Grudge (2004) and Dark Water (2005)
Samara is the adopted daughter of Richard and Anna Morgan
Sequel The Ring Two released 2005

films.title: Resident Evil
films.yearNote: First released in Germany on March 12, 2002
films.basedOn: Resident Evil (Capcom video game series)
films.villain: The Umbrella Corporation's T-virus zombies, and the Red Queen AI that seals the Hive
notes: First film in the Resident Evil series; five sequels followed (Apocalypse 2004 through The Final Chapter 2016)
Principal photography began March 5, 2001 in Berlin, including U-Bahnhof Bundestag
German studio Constantin Film bought the rights to adapt the series
Released in the UK on July 12, 2002

films.title: Signs
films.villain: Alien invaders who appear after crop circles
notes: Joaquin Phoenix was cast a week before filming after Mark Ruffalo needed surgery for a tumor
Mel Gibson plays a former Episcopal priest who lost his wife
Biggest opening weekend of Mel Gibson's career at the time, surpassing Ransom
Released August 2, 2002

films.title: Cabin Fever
films.yearNote: Premiered at TIFF on September 14, 2002; U.S. release September 12, 2003
films.villain: An unknown flesh-eating disease
notes: Eli Roth's directorial debut
Principal photography in North Carolina in late 2001
Script inspired by The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, The Last House on the Left and The Evil Dead
Franchise includes Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever (2009), Patient Zero (2014) and a 2016 remake

films.title: Ju-On: The Grudge
films.yearNote: Premiered at Screamfest October 18, 2002; Japan release August 23, 2003
films.villain: The vengeful ghosts of Kayako Saeki and her son Toshio
notes: Third installment in the Ju-on series and the first released theatrically (the first two were direct-to-video)
Takeo Saeki murders wife Kayako and son Toshio, creating the curse
Narrative is presented nonlinearly
Spawned a franchise, an American remake, and the prequel series Ju-On: Origins (2020)

films.title: Blade II
films.basedOn: Blade (Marvel Comics) by Marv Wolfman and Gene Colan
films.villain: Jared Nomak, a Reaper-virus carrier created by Eli Damaskinos
notes: Sequel to Blade (1998)
Blade joins the vampire 'Bloodpack' to fight the Reapers
Released March 22, 2002
Nominated at the 29th Saturn Awards

films.title: Queen of the Damned
films.basedOn: The Queen of the Damned (1988 novel) by Anne Rice
films.villain: Akasha, the ancient vampire queen awakened by Lestat's music
notes: Aaliyah's final film role
Aaliyah, who debuted in Romeo Must Die, was the first actor cast
Stand-alone sequel to Interview with the Vampire (1994) in the Vampire Chronicles
Released February 22, 2002 (U.S.); Australia/US co-production

films.title: Ghost Ship
films.setting: Bering Sea; ocean liner Antonia Graza
films.villain: Jack Ferriman, a demonic spirit who lures sinners to Hell; ghost of Francesca
notes: Salvage crew finds the Italian liner Antonia Graza, missing since 1962
A Dark Castle Entertainment production
Steve Beck's second film after Thir13en Ghosts
Released October 25, 2002

films.title: Dog Soldiers
films.villain: A pack of werewolves attacking a squad of soldiers on a training exercise
notes: Neil Marshall's feature directorial debut; he also wrote and edited it
Released in the UK on 10 May 2002
Simon Pegg was offered the role of Spoon but had promised Edgar Wright that Shaun of the Dead would be his first film role
Launched Marshall's career

films.title: Dark Water
films.basedOn: 'Floating Water' (1996 short story) by Koji Suzuki
films.villain: The ghost of a girl, Mitsuko Kawai, haunting the apartment
notes: Released January 19, 2002
Directed by Hideo Nakata
American remake directed by Walter Salles with Jennifer Connelly and Tim Roth, released July 8, 2005

films.title: May
films.yearNote: Premiered at Sundance January 13, 2002; U.S. release February 7, 2003
films.villain: May Canady, a lonely veterinary assistant traumatized by childhood bullying
notes: Lucky McKee's directorial debut
Lionsgate bought worldwide distribution rights at Sundance for about $800,000
May works as a veterinary assistant and was bullied as a child over a lazy eye

films.title: Below
films.villain: Supernatural presence haunting the submarine
notes: Co-written by Darren Aronofsky, a producer through Protozoa Pictures
Released October 11, 2002 by Miramax (Dimension Films production)
Set aboard a WWII U.S. Navy submarine

films.title: Valentine
films.basedOn: Valentine (1997 novel) by Tom Savage
films.villain: A killer wearing a Cupid mask who stalks childhood friends before Valentine's Day
notes: Shot in Vancouver in the summer of 2000
US/Canada/Australia co-production
Released February 2, 2001 in the U.S.
Opening scene set in 1988 at a junior high Valentine's dance

films.title: Frailty
films.yearNote: Premiered at Deep Ellum Film Festival November 7, 2001; U.S. release April 12, 2002
films.villain: Dad Meiks, a father who says an angel told him to destroy demons disguised as humans
notes: Bill Paxton's directorial debut
The 'God's Hand' serial killings frame the story
Story is set in 1979 and the present

films.title: What Lies Beneath
films.writers: Clark Gregg (story by Kernochan and Gregg)
films.villain: A female ghost haunting the Spencers' home (Madison Frank); revealed to be linked to Norman
notes: Original story by Sarah Kernochan, inspired by a real paranormal experience she had
Zemeckis shot it during a hiatus from filming Cast Away (2000)
First film produced by Zemeckis's ImageMovers after it was rebranded from South Side Amusement Company
Filmed on location in Vermont and on soundstages in Los Angeles

films.title: Scream 3
films.basedOn: Characters created by Kevin Williamson
films.villain: A new Ghostface killing the cast of the film-within-a-film Stab 3
notes: Third installment of the Scream series
Opened at number one with $34.7M, breaking the February weekend-debut record held by The Empire Strikes Back: Special Edition
Kevin Williamson gave a five-page outline for two sequels when auctioning his original script
Principal photography July to September 1999; ending re-filmed January 2000
Roger L. Jackson voices Ghostface

films.title: Hollow Man
films.villain: Sebastian Caine, a scientist who turns violent after making himself invisible
notes: Debuted at number one on August 4, 2000
Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects at the 73rd Academy Awards
Filmed in California and the Washington, D.C. area
Direct-to-video sequel Hollow Man 2 (2006) starred Christian Slater

films.title: The Cell
films.villain: Carl Rudolph Stargher, a comatose serial killer whose mind Catherine enters
notes: Tarsem Singh's feature directorial debut
Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Makeup and four Saturn Awards
A scene with a horse split by glass panels was inspired by Damien Hirst
Released August 18, 2000

films.title: Shadow of the Vampire
films.villain: Max Schreck, who plays Count Orlok and is secretly a real vampire
notes: Fictionalized account of the making of Nosferatu (1922)
Nominated at the 73rd Academy Awards for Best Makeup and Best Supporting Actor (Dafoe)
Co-production of BBC Films and Nicolas Cage's Saturn Films; shot in Luxembourg
Premiered at Cannes May 15, 2000

films.title: Pitch Black
altTitles: The Chronicles of Riddick: Pitch Black
films.writers: Ken Wheat, Jim Wheat and David Twohy
films.villain: Predatory flying creatures that emerge during a total eclipse
notes: Final film credit of PolyGram Filmed Entertainment
Sequel The Chronicles of Riddick released 2004
Riddick (2013) was a later sequel
Released February 18, 2000

films.title: Urban Legends: Final Cut
films.writers: Paul Harris Boardman and Scott Derrickson
films.basedOn: Urban Legend (1998) by Silvio Horta (characters)
films.villain: A killer targeting film students using urban-legend-style murders
notes: John Ottman's directorial debut; he also edited and composed
Sequel to Urban Legend (1998)
Followed by direct-to-video Urban Legends: Bloody Mary (2005)

films.title: Jason X
films.yearNote: Released in Spain November 15, 2001; U.S. release April 26, 2002
films.basedOn: Characters by Victor Miller
films.villain: Jason Voorhees, revived from cryogenic freezing in space
notes: Tenth installment of the Friday the 13th franchise
Kane Hodder's fourth and final appearance as Jason
Jason is captured in 2008 and frozen at the Crystal Lake Research Facility

films.title: Halloween: Resurrection
films.basedOn: Characters created by Debra Hill and John Carpenter
films.villain: Michael Myers
notes: Eighth installment of the Halloween franchise; sequel to Halloween H20 (1998)
Final installment of the H20 timeline
Idea inspired by the rise of reality television
Released July 12, 2002

films.title: The Devil's Backbone
films.writers: del Toro, David Muñoz and A. Trashorras
films.villain: The ghost 'Santi', and the groundskeeper Jacinto
notes: Released April 20, 2001 in Spain
Fernando Tielve's film debut
Tielve and Íñigo Garcés later cameoed as guerrilla soldiers in Pan's Labyrinth (2006)
Nominated for Saturn Awards

films.title: Dracula 2000
films.basedOn: Dracula (1897 novel) by Bram Stoker
films.villain: Dracula, revealed to be Judas Iscariot
notes: Reveals Dracula's origin as Judas Iscariot
Principal photography took place on location in New Orleans
Released December 22, 2000
Followed by direct-to-video sequels Ascension (2003) and Legacy (2005)

films.title: FearDotCom
films.villain: Vengeful spirit of Jeannie Richardson powering the 'feardotcom' site; serial killer Alistair Pratt
notes: Victims have 48 hours to live after viewing the site
Principal photography in Luxembourg and Montreal
Released August 30, 2002

films.title: Red Dragon
films.basedOn: Red Dragon (1981 novel) by Thomas Harris
films.villain: Francis Dolarhyde, the 'Tooth Fairy', driven by his alter ego the Great Red Dragon
notes: Ted Tally, who wrote The Silence of the Lambs, returned after turning down Hannibal (2001)
Score by Danny Elfman
Premiered September 30, 2002 at the Ziegfeld Theatre; U.S. release October 4, 2002
Nominated for Saturn Awards

films.title: The Eye
films.director: Danny Pang and Oxide Pang (the Pang brothers)
films.writers: Jojo Hui and the Pang brothers
films.villain: Ghosts seen by violinist Wong Kar-mun after a cornea transplant
notes: Released May 9, 2002 in Hong Kong
Spawned sequels The Eye 2 and The Eye 10
Remade in Tamil (Adhu, 2004), Hindi (Naina, 2005) and as The Eye (2008) with Jessica Alba

films.title: Ichi the Killer
films.basedOn: Ichi the Killer (manga) by Hideo Yamamoto
films.distributor: Prénom H Co, Ltd. (Japan); Media Blasters (US)
films.villain: Ichi, a psychotic man manipulated by his handler Jijii
notes: Premiered at TIFF September 14, 2001; Japan release December 22, 2001
Based on Hideo Yamamoto's manga
Directed by Takashi Miike

films.title: Uzumaki
films.basedOn: Uzumaki (manga) by Junji Ito
films.villain: A spiral curse afflicting the town
notes: Released February 11, 2000 in Japan
Director Higuchinsky's directorial debut (real name Akihiro Higuchi)
Based on Junji Ito's manga

films.title: Eight Legged Freaks
films.villain: Giant mutated spiders exposed to toxic waste
notes: Originally titled Arac Attack; released under that title in parts of Europe
Cast includes Scarlett Johansson
Released July 19, 2002 in the U.S.

films.title: Bubba Ho-Tep
films.basedOn: Bubba Ho-Tep (novella) by Joe R. Lansdale
films.setting: Shady Rest Retirement Home, East Texas
films.villain: Bubba Ho-Tep, an ancient Egyptian mummy terrorizing a retirement home
notes: Reggie Bannister of the Phantasm series cameos
Elvis and JFK are nursing home residents
Released September 19, 2002

films.title: Hannibal
films.genreNote: psychological thriller / Silence of the Lambs sequel
films.basedOn: Hannibal (1999 novel) by Thomas Harris
films.villain: Hannibal Lecter; Mason Verger, Lecter's surviving victim
notes: Sequel to The Silence of the Lambs (1991)
Julianne Moore replaced Jodie Foster as Starling
Principal photography began May 2000 and lasted sixteen weeks
Released February 9, 2001

films.title: They
films.villain: Creatures from the dark behind characters' night terrors
notes: Also known as Wes Craven Presents: They
Radar Pictures' first film production
Released November 27, 2002

films.title: Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2
films.genreNote: sequel to The Blair Witch Project
films.villain: The Blair Witch legacy; Jeff's group visits Rustin Parr's house
notes: Sequel to The Blair Witch Project
Released October 27, 2000
Directed and co-written by documentarian Joe Berlinger
Opens in November 1999 in Burkittsville, Maryland

unverified: American Psycho: fetched article lead text named a different director ('Georgia May Russell-Allen'), contradicting the infobox and history; used Mary Harron per infobox (likely article vandalism at fetch time).

Ginger Snaps (premiere Munich Aug 2000, wide release May 2001), Cabin Fever (TIFF Sept 2002, US Sept 2003), May (Sundance Jan 2002, US 2003), Ju-On: The Grudge (Screamfest Oct 2002, Japan Aug 2003), Frailty (Deep Ellum Nov 2001, US Apr 2002), Jason X (Spain Nov 2001, US Apr 2002), Resident Evil (Germany Mar 2002) and Ichi the Killer (TIFF Sept 2001): year taken from the earliest release date in the infobox; see yearNote.
Ju-on: The Grudge: article title says 2002 film; Japanese theatrical release listed Aug 2003, so year may be disputed by other sources.

The Eye box office left empty (article figure truncated 'HK$13,733,'). May box office left empty (article figure truncated '$634,'); budget only noted in file as $1.7M but boxOffice field was set to '$1.7M budget' - treat as budget only.

Cast lists are limited to each article's cast section; settings left blank where the article did not state one (Scary Movie, Queen of the Damned, The Cell, May, They, Red Dragon, The Eye). The Eye and May box office left empty because the fetched article figures were truncated.

Seeds excluded for year: Final Destination 2 (2003), Ginger Snaps 2 (2004), Cube (1997), Bats and Lake Placid (1999), Wishmaster (1997). Not researched: Dagon (2001), Darkness (2002), Trouble Every Day (2001), Versus (2000), Hellraiser: Inferno (2000), Lost Souls (2000), The Mummy Returns (2001), Series 7 (2001).
Villain and short field wording are paraphrased from plot summaries; Valentine's killer identity not recorded.
